summary.en: The Philippine Coast Guard contained a 2,000‑liter mineral oil leak from a submarine cable off Tabango, Leyte, while Japan pledged $27 million for coastal radar and drones to boost Philippine surveillance. China Coast Guard vessels continued patrolling waters around the disputed Diaoyu Dao and a Chinese survey ship entered Scarborough Shoal, prompting the Philippines to summon the Chinese ambassador over remarks it deemed threatening. Manila also sought additional Indian BrahMos missiles to strengthen its coastal defenses against China. 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den filippinske kystvakten stoppet et 2 000‑liter mineraloljelekkasje fra en undervannskabel utenfor Tabango, Leyte, mens Japan lovet 27 millioner dollar til kystradar og droner for å styrke Filippinenes overvåkning. Kystvakten i Kina fortsatte patruljeringen av farvannene rundt den omstridte Diaoyu-øyen, og et kinesisk undersøkelsesfartøy gikk inn i Scarborough-revet, noe som fikk Filippinene til å innkalle den kinesiske ambassadøren etter bemerkninger de anså som truende. Manila søkte også om flere indiske BrahMos-missiler for å styrke kystforsvaret mot Kina. 176 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Moro conflict
background.extract: The Moro conflict was an insurgency in the Mindanao region in southern Philippines which involved multiple armed groups. A decades-long peace process has resulted in peace deals between the Philippine government and two major armed groups, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), but other smaller armed groups continue to exist. In 2017, the peace council settled around 138 clan conflicts.
